title: How to get into ai-gamedev for free?
author: Any-Landscape434
selftext:
From the code to the art, sounds/music, and such, how can one make a whole game using mostly ai for the heavy lifting without spending nothing? assume i have your average type of computer not low end but not high end either.

What tools can i use if any? anything you wish to add or say?

comments.author: corysama
comments.body: What GPU do you have?  There are free tools you can run on your own machine. But, you’ll need a machine to run them on.

replies.author: Any-Landscape434
replies.body:
i have a rtx 3060 (12vram), 16gb of ddr4, a intel xeon cpu.

Those are the basic specs of my computer right now.

comments.author: Disposable110
comments.body: Opencode / Pidev and then load a free AI model in vllm / llamacpp / oobabooga and set it as custom provider in opencode.

comments.author: KreemPeynir
comments.body:
I'm using AI for free as well.  
If you are a student look for a student free trials, or general free trails too. Although the general free trials are usually just 1 month and not enough imo. I able to get gemini pro for 1 year as a student.

If you couldn't find it. Use Cline + API on VScode.  
There are lots of APIs with limited free useage. You can switch in between them too.

For art, you can still try to use free daily image generation limit with chatgpt and gemini.   
But I recommend local image generation such as Stable Diffision, Z image or Flux.2 etc.   
It still requires you to have a good GPU tho.

For music, there's a local Music generator as well, Ace Step. Online free trials ones usually have lisance problems, so I won't recommend them.

comments.author: Darknessborn
comments.body: Important to note that unless you're doing it offline (ie local models) be careful about the terms of use for free trials, just prohibit commercial use so you can't make money off it. I ran into this issue with Suno

replies.author: WhitleyxNeo
replies.body:
That's one of the things I was afraid of 

I want to learn the basics of coding first before I start using AI otherwise if something is broken I won't know how to fit it

replies.author: Darknessborn
replies.body: Honestly not much point learning to code now. As long as you get basic logic and the overall framework of coding (variables, functions, if/else, loops, etc) you're better off spending your time building and breaking apps

replies.author: WhitleyxNeo
replies.body: It's always good to learn the basics though

replies.author: Darknessborn
replies.body: Yeah basics like the stuff I listed but less so actual languages these days

comments.author: nievinny
comments.body:
You can't. Do not listen to anyone telling you otherwise. Good models cost money they are for profit companies it's not a red cross. 

That's said you should go far spending around 200$ a month. With Claude and Gemini. Maybe few others but those 2 are good to start.

After all it's not much for the benefit you are getting.

Though there is one elephant in the room that is not mentioned in the thread, and it looks like you may not be aware of.
As some who spent years in gamedev and VFX working on many AAA productions. Trust me, It was never hard to do a game, even before AI. It is hard to sell one.

replies.author: sirpalee
replies.body:
There is a huge gap between local models on a lower spec (lower spec when talking about running ai) and paid big models. Well worth the 200$ a month.

However it looks like the 200$ subscriptions are being taken away or scaled down and we'll likely see a more expensive tier being normalized, due to all the agentic use.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: Lots of tools have some free credits every day. Leonardo, all the chatGPT equivalents..

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
local AI is a really good option if you are tech savvy to install stuff and you have a powerful machine. 

since you dont, google all kinds of AIs. look for another one if it is not free. That's it, really. 

tons of people are vibe coding their AI apps so currently there are full of free-ish AI tools. 

this sub has those advertisements too. just pay attention next time when someone say "check out this app or that app"

comments.author: Constant_Physics8504
comments.body: All aspects of game dev no, but if you want to code single player games that require no backend yes you can. Things like flappy bird, brick break, Tetris etc

comments.body: We just launched freemium on Tesana.ai with daily credit resets, I can add some credits on your account too if you want to make a game to get into it!

comments.author: Bluetails_Buizel
comments.body: JavaScript + germini + learn JavaScript + germini to make simple games that are not confined within the scratch / Roblox ecosystem.

comments.author: Emergency_Mastodon56
comments.body: Pick up unreal engine (free), join the beta for logicsmith (free). Beta.logicsmith.dev
